claims.text: High configurational entropy slows bulk diffusion in high-entropy alloys.
Sluggish bulk diffusion retains Al in the subsurface and prevents rapid Al depletion from the alloy interior.
Retained subsurface Al selectively segregates to the surface during high-temperature oxidation.
Surface-segregated Al forms a continuous and adherent Al2O3 layer.
A dense, stable Al2O3 scale protects the underlying alloy during high-temperature oxidation.
Homogenization or related microstructural adjustments can produce variants with different mixing entropy while leaving total Al concentration unchanged.
Varying mixing entropy at constant Al content isolates an entropy-driven Al retention and segregation effect.
At constant Al content, alloys with higher effective mixing entropy will show greater surface Al segregation than the baseline.
At constant Al content, alloys with higher effective mixing entropy will form a thicker Al2O3 scale than the baseline.
At constant Al content, alloys with higher effective mixing entropy will form a more uniform Al2O3 scale than the baseline.
At constant Al content, alloys with higher effective mixing entropy will form a more adherent Al2O3 scale than the baseline.
The baseline alloy has more rapid Al depletion and consequently forms a less uniform and less protective oxide.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply during isothermal oxidation at 900–950°C for 100 hours under fixed oxygen partial pressure.
The mechanism may not extend directly to cyclic oxidation or atmospheres with changing reactive-gas composition.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mechanism require entropy variants to be compared at constant Al content, but the falsification design describes a control set in which oxide-scale differences are attributed solely to altered Al content. This does not provide the stated constant-Al control.

The mechanism invokes slower bulk diffusion to retain Al, yet also predicts enhanced delivery or segregation of subsurface Al to the surface. The hypothesis does not explain how reduced Al transport simultaneously produces greater surface enrichment.

The material is described as an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi matrix with additional controlled Al, but neither the Al concentration nor how equiatomicity is maintained after adding Al is specified. The proposed compositional adjustments also conflict with the requirement that only entropy, and not relevant composition, be varied.
